explanation: The V32I mutation introduces a ~27 Ų volume expansion in the S2/S2' subpocket while maintaining hydrophobic character, creating a steric clash that directly impedes darunavir positioning at a critical contact point only 4.1 Å from the ligand. The enlarged isoleucine side chain disrupts the precise van der Waals packing geometry that darunavir requires for optimal binding in this constrained region, forcing the inhibitor into a suboptimal conformation or partial displacement that destabilizes the inhibitor-protease complex.
